messages:
maria: Quick sync — sales pushed back on the new SKU reshuffle. They want a middle-tier that keeps existing commit economics but adds a small QoS addon for priority routing. Can product ops and legal confirm constraints?

jonathan: Do we have capacity/SLAs for an intermediate QoS lane? Even a small addon still needs routing guarantees.

kevin: Capacity-wise we can support a soft-priority lane, but two constraints: 1) must not change existing reserved capacity contracts' headroom; 2) billing mapping needs to be unambiguous (credits vs per-token).

sarah: +1 from AE side — two pilot customers asked specifically for "priority burst" that doesn't require upgrading to Dedicated. They want predictable monthly pricing and a contract clause limiting monthly peak usage above baseline.

ethan: For rollout gating, can we require: docs + pricing matrix + migration path + telemetry? Metrics: error rate <= 0.5% at p99 latency target, and <10% of requests routed to fallback variant in first 2 weeks.

maria: Proposed launch criteria checklist: 
- Pricing SKU and per-addon MRR mapped in billing system
- Contract language (softcap, overage calc, priority definition) signed off by legal
- Console UI for enabling addon + tenant-level toggle + enforcement
- Backwards-compatible behavior for existing customers (no silent rate changes)
- Pilot with 2 customers and metrics guardrails

jonathan: Important: define "priority routing" precisely. Example snippet for legal/eng:
```
priority routing = best-effort pref to dedicated pool A for buckets with addon flag set; fallback to shared pool B when A is saturated; burst cap = X tokens/min per tenant; overage = billed monthly at Y rate
```

kevin: Overage calc must align with commit contracts. If a customer has reserved capacity, their addon should either draw from reserved pool first or be entirely billed as addon consumption on top — can't mix and match without explicit clause.

sarah: Customers will push for crediting their burst back into their commit. We should prepare negotiation playbook: standard = addon billed separately; negotiable = apply to commit up to cap for 12 months.

sam-bot: Reminder: please update the product spec doc (PR #4321) after this thread.

ethan: Also: telemetry hooks needed — per-tenant routing logs + per-route p99 + fallback rate. Ops needs those to validate SLA and to run canary.

maria: Action items: @kevin draft contract language options by EOD Wed; @ethan mock telemetry schema and alert thresholds by Thu; @jonathan confirm capacity with infra and provide burst cap numbers; @sarah collect the two pilot customers' exact usage patterns.

jonathan: I'll confirm with infra — quick estimate: safe initial burst cap ~ 500k tokens/min per tenant (subject to final perf tests).

maria: Cool — we'll reconvene Fri 10am to decide whether to proceed with pilot or pivot to a credit-based offering. :thumbsup:

sarah: Thanks everyone — I'll line up the pilot NDAs and customer brief.
